statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = z\vec k through the parameterized surface S, which is oriented toward the z-axis and given, for 0\leq s \leq 2, \ \ 0\leq t\leq 1, by x = 5 s + 2 t, \quad y = 5 s - 2 t, \quad z = s^2+t^2.

static.solution: S is given by \vec r (s,t) = (5 s+ 2 t)\vec i + (5 s- 2 t)\vec j + (s^2+t^2)\vec k, we have \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} = 5\vec i + 5 \vec j +2 s\vec k \quad\hbox{ and }\quad \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} = 2 \vec i - 2 \vec j + 2t\vec k, and \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} \times \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ 5 \amp 5 \amp 2s\\ 2 \amp -2 \amp 2t \end{array}\right| = (4 s+ 10 t)\vec i +(4 s - 10 t)\vec j - 20 \vec k. Since the \vec i component of this vector is positive for 0 \lt s \lt 2, 0 \lt t \lt 1, it points away from the z-axis, and so has the opposite orientation to the one specified. Thus, we use d\vec A = - \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} \times \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t} \, ds \, dt, and so we have \int_S \vec F\cdot d\vec A = -\int_0^{1}\int_0^{2} (s^2+t^2)\vec k \cdot \left( (4 s+ 10 t)\vec i +(4 s - 10 t)\vec j - 20 \vec k\right) \,ds\,dt = 20\int_0^{1}\int_0^{2}(s^2+t^2)\,ds\,dt = 20\int_0^{1} \left(\frac{s^3}3+st^2\right) \bigg|_{s=0}^{s=2}\,dt = 20\int_0^{1}(\frac{8}{3} + 2 t^2)\,dt = 20(\frac{8}{3} t+ \frac{2}{3} t^3\bigg|_0^{1} = 20(\frac{8}{3} + \frac{2}{3}) = \frac{200}{3}.
